full_judgment:
Zinat Ara J : In this application under article 102 of the Constitution the petitioners called in question the legality of the order dated 23-11-2008 passed by the learned Judge of Artha Rin Adalat and Joint District Judge, Court No. 1, Jessore in Misc . Case No. 117 of 2008 (Annexure-E to the Writ Petition) rejecting an application tiled by the petitioners under section 19 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. 

 3. Petitioner No. 1 Messrs Trade Multi flex and its proprietors petitioner No. 2 Rashed Mehluz Khan took loan of an amount of Taka 4,80,000 from Janata Bank Ltd., Corporate Branch, MK Road. Jessore (hereinafter referred to as the Bank). The loan was subsequently enhanced by-the Bank from time to time. The petitioners repaid some amount of loan on several dates but from the first part of 2006, the petitioners started facing huge loss in the business due to political unrest and others environmental unavoidable circumstances and therefore, they could not pay the loan. Subsequently, the Bank filed Artha Rin Suit No. 45 of 2007 before the Artha Rin Adalat and Joint District Judge, Court No. 1, Jessore (shortly, the Adalat) on 27-6-2007 for recovery of Taka 11,59,455. The petitioners did not receive the summons of the suit as result of which they could not appear to contest the suit and the suit was ultimately decreed exparte by judgment and decree dated 2-1-2008. Thereafter, the Bank tiled Artha Jari Case No. 41 of 2008 before the Adalat. The Petitioners came to know about the exparte decree and execution case on 26-10-2008 and instantly filed an application under section 19 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (shortly, the Ain) on 28-10-2008 praying for setting aside the exparte judgment and decree. The said application was registered as Misc. Case No. 117 of 2008. In the Misc Case the Adalat by order dated 29-10-2008 directing the judgment-debtor-petitioners to deposit 10% of the decretal amount within 15 days. Accordingly, the petitioners deposited the said amount on 10-11-2008 but the learned Judge of the Adalat subsequently by the impugned order dated 23-11-2008 disallowed the Misc. Case on the ground of limitation, where-upon this writ petition has been filed by the petitioners and the rule was obtained. 

 4. Respondent No. 2, the Bank contested the rule by filing an affidavit-in-opposition denying the materials averments made in the writ petition contending inter alia, that all the defendants of Artha Rin Suit No. 45 of 2003 reside together in the same house. Defendant No. 5 is the mother of defendants Nos. 2-4 of the Artha Rin Suit. Being satisfied with the services of summons/notices in accordance with law, the learned Judge of the Adalat fixed a date for exparte hearing of the suit on 1-9-2007. Defendant No. 5 (petitioner No. 2's mother) appeared in the suit on 12-9-2007 and prayed for time for submitting written statement which was allowed with cost of Taka 5,000. The petitioners also appeared in the Artha Rin Suit No. 45 of 2007 and prayed for time to file written statement which was also allowed but the petitioners did not file any written statement on the next dates i.e. 19-9-2007 and 22-10-2007. Thereafter, date was fixed for exparte hearing on 31-10-2007 but again the Adalat allowed chance to the petitioners to file written statement on 31-10-2007 and 13-11-2007 but the petitioners and the defendant No. 5 did not file written statement and therefore, the suit was decreed exparte on 2-1-2008. It is evident from the record that the petitioners were well aware about the Artha Rin Suit No. 45 of 2003 since 19-9-2003 and so, the learned Judge of the Adalat rejected the Misc. Case in accordance with law. The writ petition is misconceived, not maintainable and thus, the rule is liable to be discharged. 

 6. The petitioners also filed an affidavit-1 reply to the affidavit-in-oppositions contenting, inter alia, that defendant Nos. 1-5 neither received any summons of Artha Rin Suit No. 45 of 2003 nor they appeared before the Adalat at any time. So the appearance of the petitioners and the defendant No. 5 in the Artha Rin Suit are act of forgery committed by some interested quarters and the petitioners had no knowledge about the exparte judgment and decree and execution case. 

 7. Mr Ali Imam Khaled Rahim, the learned Advocate for the petitioners submits that the petitioners and defendant No. 5 did not receive any summons of the suit and therefore, they were and able to appear in the suit and contest it which resulted in the exparte judgment and decree and the petitioners had no knowledge about filing of the execution case. He next submits that defendant No.5 the mother of the petitioner No. 2 as well as the petitioners did not appears in the Artha Rin Sit ad if their appearance is shown' in the suit those are acts of forgery committed by interested quarters. He lastly submits that after knowing about the judgment and decree as well as about the execution case the petitioners immediately appeared before the Adalat and filed an application under section 19 of the Ain for restoration of the suit setting aside the ex-parte judgment and decree and the petitioners also deposited 10% of the decretal dues as per order of the Adalat but the learned Judge of the Adalat without deciding the claim of the petitioners on merit on taking evidence rejected the Misc. Case holding illegally that the petitioners were well aware about the filing of the suit long before and the Misc. Case 'was barred. by limitation and therefore, the rule is liable to be made absolute. 

 11. It has been categorically stated in the application tiled by the petitioners under section 19 of the Ain (Annexure-D to the Writ Petition) that the petitioners did not receive any summons/notices as a result of which they could not appears in the suit or in the execution case earlier. 

 12. Form the affidavit-in-opposition filed by the Bank, it appears that the defendant No. 5 moth-er of the petitioner appeared but it has been claimed by the petitioners by filing an affidavit-in-reply that defendant No. 5 or the other defendants never appeared in the suit or in the execution case and their appearance if shown in the suit, are act of forgery by some interested quarters. 

 13. Be that as it may, the question as to whether the petitioners and defendant No. 5 appeared to contest the suit or no being disputed question of fact cannot be decided in writ jurisdiction without taking evidence. Moreover, the petitioners filed this writ petition against an order dated 23-11-2008 disallowing the Misc Case No. 117 of 2008 filed under section 19 of the Ain. Therefore, the petitioners remedy is before the appellate forum in view of the provision of section 41 of the Ain. 

 14. Furthermore, it has been decided in an unreported case by judgment dated 17-8-2010 passed in Writ Petition No. 5746 of 2005 (the Oriental Bank Ltd vs Artha Rin Adalat No. 4, Dhaka and others) by this Division as under: 

 "Therefore, it transpires that section 41(1) of the Ain provides that if any party to a Manila is aggrieved by an order or decree, he is to prefer an appeal against the said order or decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat within 30 days. Under section 44 of the Ain interlocutory orders passed by the Artha Rin Adalat cannot be challenged in appellate and revisional jurisdiction and so, writ petitions are maintainable against interlocutory orders passed by the Artha Rin Adalat. Therefore, it transpires that the orders passed by the Artha Rin Adalat which are not interlocutory orders are appellate orders inasmuch as the words' order or decree" it has used in sub-section (1) of section 41 of the Ain. On going through the entire provisions of section 41 of the Ain it does not appears that the word" order" is meant only for the orders passed under section 19(2) of the Ain. Therefore, the order rejecting of execution case being a final order of the Adalat, the petitioner is to file an appeal against said order and the writ petition is not maintainable." 

 15. The view taken in the said decision is also applicable in the instant case. In view of the above, we find that this writ petition is not maintainable. As it is found that this it petition is not maintainable, we do not like to embark upon the order issues touching the merit thereof.
